chunks: Yūnus, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The thief is not subjected to amputation except for something whose value reaches that of a shield, and that is a quarter of a dīnār."

key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief; the person who commits theft
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: a quarter of a dīnār; the stated minimum legal threshold
key_terms.قِيمَتُهُ: its value; the monetary worth of the stolen item
key_terms.مِجَنًّا: a shield; used here as a measure of value
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: is subjected to amputation as the legal hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen property for the theft hadd to apply in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal threshold for the hadd punishment of theft. It clarifies that amputation is not carried out unless the stolen item's value reaches the equivalent of a shield, defined here as a quarter of a dīnār.
